=== FILE: 5 Rationalistic Criticisms.md ===
# 5 Rationalistic Criticisms

Messrs. Schiller's and Dewey's theories have suffered a hailstorm of contempt and ridicule. All rationalism has risen against them. A hailstorm of contempt and ridicule{} throws so much sidelight upon that rationalistic temper to which I{, }William James{, }have opposed the temper of pragmatism. Pragmatism is uncomfortable away from facts. Rationalism is comfortable only in the presence of abstractions. This pragmatist talk about truths in the plural, about their utility and satisfactoriness, about the success with which they 'work,' etc., suggests to the typical intellectualist mind a sort of coarse lame second-rate makeshift article of truth. Such truths are not real truth. Such tests are merely subjective. As against this, objective truth must be something non-utilitarian, haughty, refined, remote, august, exalted. It must be an absolute correspondence of our thoughts with an equally absolute reality. It must be what we OUGHT to think, unconditionally. The conditioned ways in which we DO think are so much irrelevance and matter for psychology. Down with psychology, up with logic, in all this question!

The pragmatist clings to facts and concreteness, observes truth at its work in particular cases, and generalizes. Truth, for him, becomes a class-name for all sorts of definite working-values in experience. For the rationalist it remains a pure abstraction, to the bare name of which we must defer. When the pragmatist undertakes to show in detail just WHY we must defer, the rationalist is unable to recognize the concretes from which his own abstraction is taken. He accuses us{, }Messrs. Dewey, Schiller and their allies{, }of DENYING truth; whereas we have only sought to trace exactly why people follow it and always ought to follow it. Your typical ultra-abstractionist fairly shudders at concreteness: other things equal, he positively prefers the pale and spectral.

Pragmatism{} only follows here the example of the sister-sciences, interpreting the unobserved by the observed. It brings old and new harmoniously together. It converts the absolutely empty notion of a static relation of 'correspondence'{} between our minds and reality, into that of a rich and active commerce (that anyone may follow in detail and understand) between particular thoughts of ours, and the great universe of other experiences in which they play their parts and have their uses.
=== REPORT ===
Dangling-reference repairs:

- "Messrs. Schiller's and Dewey's theories have suffered a hailstorm…": the reader framing "You will probably be surprised to learn, then, that" was cut. This was a first-person/pointing cut.
- "…throws so much sidelight upon that rationalistic temper…": I made three repairs here.
  - "I should not mention this, but for the fact that" was cut as first-person framing.
  - "it" was replaced by the name span "a hailstorm of contempt and ridicule", with the first letter capitalised.
  - "I" got the author name span "William James", taken from the `source:` line.
- "He accuses us … whereas we have only sought…": "us" and "we" mean the pragmatists as a specific group. I appended the name span "Messrs. Dewey, Schiller and their allies", taken from the frame's segment "History of the Method"/"Pragmatism as a Theory of Truth" paragraph. That also resolves the "we" later in the same sentence.
- "Pragmatism only follows here the example…": "It" lost its antecedent once the preceding "I hope…" sentence was dropped. I replaced it with the name span "pragmatism", from that dropped sentence's phrase "the pragmatism which they advocate".
- "It converts the absolutely empty notion…": the parenthetical "(what that may mean we must ask later)" was cut mid-sentence because it is a forward hook. `{}` marks the join.

"We"/"you" judged generic and left unrepaired:

- "what we OUGHT to think" and "in which we DO think": people in general, as the rationalist states the position.
- "to the bare name of which we must defer" and "just WHY we must defer": generic.
- "our thoughts", "our minds", "thoughts of ours": generic.
- "Your typical ultra-abstractionist": "you" is addressed to the reader.

Statements dropped:

- The whole first paragraph, beginning "What I have said of the theory of truth…" and ending "…respectful consideration." It is apology and forward hooks to later lectures.
- "In influential quarters Mr. Schiller, in particular, has been treated like an impudent schoolboy…": an illustration.
- "See the exquisite contrast of the types of mind!": a transition.
- "If the two universes were offered, he would always choose the skinny outline rather than the rich thicket of reality." It is a figurative illustration, and "the two universes" has no supplied referent.
- "It is so much purer, clearer, nobler.": its "It" depends on the dropped sentence before it.
- "I hope that as these lectures go on, the concreteness and closeness to facts of the pragmatism … may be what approves itself to you as its most satisfactory peculiarity." It is a forward-looking hope tied to "these lectures", and the stance is the author's first person.

Note: I read "the sister-sciences" as a general reference to the natural sciences, not as a dangling pointer, so I left it unrepaired.
